ab_tunnel_mountain.blurb: Tunnel Mountain rises practically within the town of Banff, and its cliffs are easy to reach. The climbing is nearly all bolted sport on limestone, with some multipitch sport and trad on the east side and a few boulder problems. Routes are mostly 5.9 to 5.11, with 5.10 the most common grade, a few easier lines and a handful at 5.12 and 5.13. Industrial Playground and Black Band hold the most climbs, followed by Punter Palace, The Scoop and The Wave.

bc_the_grid.blurb: The Grid is a bouldering area in the Fraser Valley of British Columbia, set in forest among large granite boulders with flat, sandy landings. Nearly all of the climbing is bouldering, from V0 up to a few very hard problems, mostly V2 to V4. The Arena holds the most climbs, a sector of closely packed boulders with good landings, followed by The Metropolis, The Back Side and The Portal. The Grid Crag is the trad part of the area, with multipitch lines.

mt_bridger_range.blurb: The Bridger Range runs roughly north to south near Bozeman in southwestern Montana. It is mostly used for skiing, biking and hiking, with climbing a newer draw, and rock quality ranges from very good to very poor. Alpine routes outnumber the sport, trad and top-rope climbs, which run mostly from 5.9 to 5.12. Wolverine Bowl holds the most climbs, with many sport routes at 5.11 to 5.12. Ross Peak is known for long alpine multipitch lines and needs an approach of one to three hours at the least. The M in Bozeman is mainly a top-rope spot.

or_rattlesnake.blurb: Rattlesnake is a sport crag in Southwest Oregon, near Medford. The cliffs are welded tuff in buttresses roughly 40 to 100 feet tall, and quality varies widely, with some loose, fractured rock low on certain longer routes. Nearly everything is bolted sport, mostly 5.10 to 5.12 with a few at 5.13. Spring and fall are the best seasons, though the crag can be climbed year round; summer is hot but shade is usually available. The Cathedral holds the most climbs, followed by Jane's Buttress and Dominator Wall, whose routes reach about 100 feet.

bc_copper_mountain.blurb: Copper Mountain, by Terrace in northern British Columbia, splits about evenly between bouldering and trad, with a smaller group of sport routes. Copper Boulders, at the base of the mountain, holds the most climbs: boulders in both sunny and shaded spots, many on flat ground at moderate heights. Problems run V0 to V4, mostly V0 to V2. Trad routes run roughly 5.7 to 5.11, mostly 5.9 and 5.10, with two-pitch lines in the Southern Dihedrals. The North End holds sport routes among others, and Perching Wall adds more.

bc_kinnaird_bluffs.blurb: Kinnaird Bluffs lies at the south end of Castlegar, British Columbia, and offers a mix of trad and sport climbing on a set of named walls. Most routes are single pitch, with a handful reaching three pitches. Grades run from about 5.5 to 5.12, with 5.10 the most common. Open Book Wall holds the most climbs and leans sport, followed by Hail Mary Wall, Yellow Sling Wall, Polished Wall and Squeeze Chimney Wall, most of them mainly trad apart from Polished Wall.
